title: Divided-power straightening for an associative sl2 triple
statement: Let $A$ be a unital associative $\mathbf Q$-algebra, equipped with the commutator Lie algebra bracket $[X,Y]=XY-YX$ [def-wf-lie-algebra], and let $E,F,H\in A$ satisfy $EF-FE=H$, $HE-EH=2E$, and $HF-FH=-2F$. For $X\in A$ and $j\in\mathbf N$ write $X^{(j)}=X^j/j!$ and $\binom{X}{j}=X(X-1)\cdots(X-j+1)/j!$, with both expressions equal to $1$ for $j=0$. For every $m,n\in\mathbf N$, one has the identity in $A$ $$E^{(m)}F^{(n)}=\sum_{t=0}^{\min(m,n)}F^{(n-t)}\binom{H-m-n+2t}{t}E^{(m-t)}.$$ No finite-dimensionality, nilpotence or faithfulness hypothesis on $A,E,F,H$ is required.

source.place: Section 23h, pp.508--510, rank-one enveloping-algebra calculation supporting integral PBW. Full source WANTED: Steinberg, Lectures on Chevalley Groups, initial integral-enveloping-algebra construction, opposite-root divided-power identity.

proof.text: Use the commutator convention of [def-wf-lie-algebra] and the three associative identities in the statement. Scalars below mean rational multiples of $1_A$ and are central. Set $B_t(X)=X(X-1)\cdots(X-t+1)/t!$ and $B_0(X)=1$; all divisions are scalar multiplication by reciprocals in $\mathbf Q$. In particular $E E^{(a)}=(a+1)E^{(a+1)}$. Rearranging the assumed relations gives $EH=(H-2)E$ and $HF=F(H-2)$.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--510 supplies the rank-one/admissible-lattice motivation only; the displayed elementary calculation is written by N7, not asserted to be proved in Milne.

proof.text: The last two identities give the required shifts directly. For $j\geq0$, $HF^j=F^j(H-2j)$: the base $j=0$ is tautological and $HF^{j+1}=F^j(H-2j)F=F^{j+1}(H-2j-2)$ proves the successor. Also $E(H+c-i)=(H+c-i-2)E$ for every rational $c$ and integer $i$. Applying this once to each of the $t$ factors in the definition gives $E B_t(H+c)=B_t(H+c-2)E$, including $t=0$.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--510 supplies the rank-one/admissible-lattice motivation only; the displayed elementary calculation is written by N7, not asserted to be proved in Milne.

proof.text:
For $r\geq1$, telescoping the product gives
$$EF^r-F^rE=\sum_{i=0}^{r-1}F^i(EF-FE)F^{r-1-i}=\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}F^{r-1}(H-2j)=rF^{r-1}(H-r+1).$$
The first sum telescopes because its $i$th summand is $F^iEF^{r-i}-F^{i+1}EF^{r-1-i}$; the middle equality uses $EF-FE=H$ and the preceding shift with $j=r-1-i$. The last sum uses $2\sum_{j=0}^{r-1}j=r(r-1)$, whose successor follows by adding $2r$. Divide by $r!$ to obtain $EF^{(r)}=F^{(r)}E+F^{(r-1)}(H-r+1)$. For $r=0$ only the first term occurs: $EF^{(0)}=E$.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--510 supplies the rank-one/admissible-lattice motivation only; the displayed elementary calculation is written by N7, not asserted to be proved in Milne.

proof.text:
For $t\geq1$ the falling products give $tB_t(X)=(X-t+1)B_{t-1}(X)$ and $B_t(X+1)-B_t(X)=B_{t-1}(X)$. Indeed the two products in the difference have the common factor $X(X-1)\cdots(X-t+2)/t!$ and their remaining factors differ by $t$. Hence, for any $m\geq0$,
$$(m+1-t)B_t(X)+(X+m-t+2)B_{t-1}(X)=(m+1)B_t(X+1).$$
To see this, replace $(X+m-t+2)B_{t-1}$ by $tB_t+(m+1)B_{t-1}$ and use the difference identity. These are identities of rational polynomials, so substitution of $H$ plus a scalar is valid without division by any element depending on $H$.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--510 supplies the rank-one/admissible-lattice motivation only; the displayed elementary calculation is written by N7, not asserted to be proved in Milne.

proof.text: Fix $n\geq0$ and induct on $m$. The base $m=0$ has exactly the term $t=0$ and reads $F^{(n)}=F^{(n)}$. Assume the displayed formula of the statement at this $m$. Multiply that equality on the left by $E$ and divide by the nonzero rational $m+1$. Since $EE^{(m)}/(m+1)=E^{(m+1)}$, this computes $E^{(m+1)}F^{(n)}$. We now expand each term of the resulting finite sum; this is equality by distributivity, not a comparison of coefficients in an assumed independent basis.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--510 supplies the rank-one/admissible-lattice motivation only; the displayed elementary calculation is written by N7, not asserted to be proved in Milne.

proof.text:
Write $C_t=H-m-n+2t$. From an old summand $F^{(n-t)}B_t(C_t)E^{(m-t)}$, where $0\leq t\leq\min(m,n)$, the first term of the formula for $EF^{(n-t)}$ and the shift give
$$\frac{m-t+1}{m+1}F^{(n-t)}B_t(C_t-2)E^{(m-t+1)}.$$
If $t<n$, the second term gives
$$\frac1{m+1}F^{(n-t-1)}(H-n+t+1)B_t(C_t)E^{(m-t)}.$$
If $t=n$ this second contribution is absent, since then $EF^{(0)}=E$. The displayed order of factors is preserved throughout; only polynomials in $H$ and rational scalars commute with each other.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--510 supplies the rank-one/admissible-lattice motivation only; the displayed elementary calculation is written by N7, not asserted to be proved in Milne.

proof.text:
Reindex the second contributions by replacing their old index with $t-1$. For $1\leq t\leq\min(m+1,n)$ put $X=H-m-n+2t-2$. The two contributions then have the common outer factors $F^{(n-t)}$ and $E^{(m+1-t)}$, with total middle factor
$$\frac{(m+1-t)B_t(X)+(X+m-t+2)B_{t-1}(X)}{m+1}=B_t(X+1).$$
Here the second coefficient is $H-n+t=X+m-t+2$. The preceding falling-product identity proves the equality. Since $X+1=H-(m+1)-n+2t$, this is exactly the middle factor required at $(m+1,n)$.

source.place: Section 23h, printed pp.508--510 supplies the rank-one/admissible-lattice motivation only; the displayed elementary calculation is written by N7, not asserted to be proved in Milne.

proof.text: Check the endpoints in that reindexing. At $t=0$ there is just the first contribution, with factor $(m+1)B_0/(m+1)=1$. At $t=m+1\leq n$ the first contribution is absent; its coefficient $m+1-t$ is zero, so the same middle-factor identity still applies to the second contribution. There is no term with $t>n$, since old index $n$ has no second contribution, and no term with $t>m+1$, since old indices are at most $m$. These observations also cover $n=0$. Thus the new range is exactly $0\leq t\leq\min(m+1,n)$, completing the induction. Only associativity, distributivity, the three relations and rational scalar arithmetic were used, so no finiteness, nilpotence, faithfulness or nonzero-triple assumption is needed.
